title: Topics in International Relations; Social Media in International Relations
description: From the Rohingya genocide to NAFO (North Atlantic Fellas Organization) and the tracking of Russian military movements during the invasion of Ukraine, social media has become an increasingly important venue for international relations. The traditional boundaries between elites and masses have become blurred and non-state groups have been able to mpact politics in a way that was previously unimaginable. This course will examine the different ways that social media has changed nternational relations and how political scientists can use new methods to examine social media with a focus on twitter. By the end of the course, students can expect a more comprehensive understanding of social media's impact on politics as well as how to scrape twitter data and analyze it.
